propositions: When a git push to the tickets branch is rejected by a policy (e.g., pre-receive hook decline / GH013 push protection), the rejection is misclassified as a non-fast-forward by the over-broad _NON_FF regex, causing the reason to be discarded and three futile retries to be executed.

A rejected auto-push returns success to the caller while leaving commits unpushed and diverged, and the failure warning is byte-identical on all subsequent writes, so an accumulating backlog remains invisible for hours unless the user manually runs git push or explicitly invokes rebar fsck.

Ticket event payloads (comments containing environment output or raw credentials) are never scanned for secrets on write, only on code review; the documented decision to scan on write at the append_event choke point exists but the implementation and refuse-vs-redact policy choice remain open in a separate ticket.

The push failure warning must preserve the literal substring 'failed after 3 retries' because existing negative assertions in test_epoch_guard_matrix.py and test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py rely on its absence.

Three delivery channels (async detached push with stderr=DEVNULL, library NullHandler, MCP tool result field) make the warning undeliverable even if it is generated, leaving sync.push=async completely silent on rejection.

The fix must classify terminal policy rejections (hook declined, protected branch, rate limit, server error, GH0) separately from retriable non-fast-forwards, report the git stderr reason and an escalating unpushed-commit count, and preserve the best-effort contract (never raise, local commit intact).
